body.content: Exploring the possibility of a 3x3 grid augmented with 4 corner points. The standard 3x3 grid (9 points) has a minimum triangle area of 0 (collinear points). If we use the 4 corners and 4 edge midpoints, we have 8 points. We need 5 more. If we place them carefully inside, we might avoid collinearity. However, the uniform grid inevitably creates very thin triangles when points are nearly collinear, making it a poor candidate for maximizing the minimum area. The optimal configuration likely involves breaking all symmetries slightly or using a completely different packing like concentric rotated squares.
body.why_keep_this: To document why naive grid augmentations fail for this specific Heilbronn-type problem.
